For discrete distributions on compatible support,

$$H(P)=-\sum_xP(x)\log P(x),\quad H(P,Q)=-\sum_xP(x)\log Q(x),$$

$$D_{KL}(P\|Q)=\sum_xP(x)\log\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}=H(P,Q)-H(P).$$

If $P$ is fixed, its entropy does not depend on model parameters, so minimizing cross-entropy over $Q_\theta$ is equivalent to minimizing forward KL. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) A zero model probability where $P$ has mass gives infinite loss. Log base determines units: natural logs give nats, base two bits. Empirical one-hot training labels approximate this population objective, but limited/noisy data and model misspecification still affect what is learned. Continuous differential entropy has additional coordinate-dependence caveats.
